extractions.quote:
Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity (PEW) characterized clinically by cerebellar ataxia, pyramidal signs and stiffness with painful muscle spasms.
Neurological examination showed a diffised permanent stiffness with lumber hyperlordosis. sparing only the face. The superimposed spasms appeared spontaneously or were triggered by unexpected noises. The patient was unable to walk because of stiffness and marked cerebellar ataxia. There were diffise hyperreflexia with bilateral Babinski sign.
CT scan of the head was normal as well as MRI of brain and spinal cord. Creatine phospho kinase (CPK) was increased to 408 UIA (normal up to 90 UVI), Ig G level in serum was 23% (normal up to 20%). Serologies for human retro-viruses (IIIV I, HTLV 1) were negative. The following antibodies were present: anti-smooth muscle at 1/640 and anti-cardiolipines at 70 UIA (normal up to
Serological studies for anti-microsomal, anti-parietal cell, anti-mitochondrial, and anti-thyroglobulin antibodies yielded negative results. HLA typing was as follows: Aw 19, A3, B44, Bw 41. Concentric needle electromyography showed continuous muscle activity in the right biceps brachialis and extensor carpi radialis longus and paraspinal cervical muscles. NO fasciculations, fibrillations or myokymias were seen. SSEPs showed decreased amplitudes with normal latencies for medullary responses. An electroencephalogram was normal. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination was normal for cell count, giu40 uin).

AN ANTI-GAD SYNDROME
FIG. 1. using as antigens human recombinant GAD I 67 and GAD II 65. Lanes 1 and 4 represent negative controls. lane 2 our Patient with PEWR and lane 3 a patient with type I diabetes mellitus. Our patient's serum shows a reactivity with both isoforms of GAD, but markedly greater with GAD II 65 than with GAD I 67. Diabetic patient's serum reacts only with GAD II 65.
cose and albumin, but Ig G level was increased by 22% without oligoclonal bands. A thorough survey of malignant markers (ACE, AFP, CA 15. 3, CA 19. 9, CT scan of the chest, intra-venous urogram, anti-HU, anti-Yo, antiCAR antibodies) was negative. A muscle biopsy was normal.
METHODS
Anti-GAD antibodies were detected in serum by ELISA using as antigens human recombinant GAD 65 and GAD 67, expressed in a eukaryotic system (Baculovirus in system SF 9). The antigens were kindly provided by ELIAS (Molecular Biology Department, Freibourg, Germany). Western Blot using the same recombinant antigens was also performed. Immunofluorescence was carried out on cryostat sections of human pancreas and monkey cerebellum.
RESULTS
Immunological studies
The following results were obtained by ELISA with the patient serum: anti-GAD 67 (GAD I) patient serum: 200 U/ml (normal sera, n = 460: 1. 6 U/ml f 4. 7), antiGAD 65 (GAD 11) patient serum: 7000 Wml (normal sera, n = 1592: 490 UVml f 1171) (Fig. 1). In Western Blot, only GAD 65 was recognized by the patient serum.
In pancreas, a strong fluorescence signal was observed, but restricted to B cells.
The specificity was demonstrated by double staining technique using anti-glucagon and anti-GAD 65 monoclonal antibodies. On monkey cerebellum, GABA-ergic nerve terminals within the molecular layer and at the base of the Purkinje cells were stained (Fig. 2).
Response to treatment
Under diazepam (40 mg daily), painful muscle jerks and diffuse stiffness completely disappeared. However, ataxia and visual condition continued to worsen. Successive trials of corticotherapy, which induced diabetes mellitus, cyclophosphamide and azathioprine were unsuccessful. In October 1993, the patient was confined to a wheelchair, visual acuity had severely deteriorated leading to blindness. No electroretinogram recording was canied out. From that time, the patient was given monthly intravenous immunoglobulin (i.v. Ig) therapy (0. 4 g/kg/day for 5 consecutive days). Following the first cure, a dra99 European Journal of Neurology . Vol 3 . 1996
After the fourth cure of i.v. Ig, she was able to walk unaided and following the sixth i.v. Ig, she reduced diazepam dosage by 30 mg without recurrence of rigidity. Her ambulation at home was only impaired by persistent blindness. This clinical state was maintained after 1 year of i.v. Ig therapy.
